name: Sun
astronomy: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star at the center of the Solar System and the closest star to Earth.
symbolism: Across many cultures, the Sun is a symbol of light, rhythm, warmth, and the visible passage of days.

name: Proxima Centauri
astronomy: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf in the Alpha Centauri system and the nearest known star to the Sun.
symbolism: Its name and proximity make it a cultural image of the near horizon within a vast sky.

name: Alpha Centauri
astronomy: Alpha Centauri is a bright multiple-star system in Centaurus, including Alpha Centauri A and B.
symbolism: As a paired stellar system, it can evoke companionship and the layered nature of a single point of light.

name: Canopus
astronomy: Canopus is a luminous yellow-white supergiant and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
symbolism: Its low southern appearance in many northern regions has made it a traditional seasonal and navigational marker.

name: Spica
astronomy: Spica is a close binary system in Virgo whose combined light makes it one of the brightest stars in the sky.
symbolism: Its association with an ear of grain in Virgo has given it a cultural connection with harvest and careful tending.

name: Fomalhaut
astronomy: Fomalhaut is a young, bright A-type star in Piscis Austrinus surrounded by a well-known debris disk.
symbolism: Its isolated autumn brightness can suggest a single clear signal in a spacious field.

name: Regulus
astronomy: Regulus is a rapidly rotating multiple-star system and the brightest star in Leo.
symbolism: Known as the heart of the Lion in Western star lore, it is a cultural image of presence and centrality.

name: Denebola
astronomy: Denebola is a young A-type main-sequence star marking the tail of Leo.
symbolism: A tail star in a recognizable constellation, it can evoke completion, motion, and a line continuing beyond sight.

name: Bellatrix
astronomy: Bellatrix is a blue giant in Orion and one of the constellation's prominent shoulder stars.
symbolism: Its place in Orion's outline has made it part of sky stories about figures, stance, and winter patterns.

name: Alnilam
astronomy: Alnilam is a blue supergiant at the center of Orion's Belt, far more luminous than the Sun.
symbolism: At the center of three aligned belt stars, it is a visual symbol of alignment and continuity.

name: Alnitak
astronomy: Alnitak is a hot multiple-star system at the eastern end of Orion's Belt near the Horsehead Nebula.
symbolism: Its position at one end of a clear asterism can evoke the first mark in a line or constellation story.

name: Mintaka
astronomy: Mintaka is a multiple-star system at the western end of Orion's Belt and lies close to the celestial equator.
symbolism: Its equatorial position and role in Orion's Belt make it a cultural image of balance and connection across hemispheres.

name: Achernar
astronomy: Achernar is a bright, rapidly rotating B-type star in Eridanus with an oblate shape caused by its rotation.
symbolism: At the end of the celestial river Eridanus, it can symbolize a journey reaching a visible edge.

name: Mirfak
astronomy: Mirfak is a yellow-white supergiant in Perseus and the brightest member of the Alpha Persei moving group.
symbolism: Its place amid a loose stellar association can evoke a bright center within a larger gathering.

name: Acrux
astronomy: Acrux is a multiple-star system and the brightest star in the Southern Cross.
symbolism: As part of a compact southern pattern, it has long served as a cultural emblem of orientation and southern skies.

name: Hyades
astronomy: The Hyades are the nearest open star cluster to the Solar System, forming a V-shaped pattern in Taurus.
symbolism: Its V-shaped face of Taurus has made it a traditional image of a familiar pattern assembled from many stars.

name: Beehive Cluster
astronomy: The Beehive Cluster, Messier 44, is an open cluster in Cancer visible to the naked eye under dark skies.
symbolism: Its swarm-like appearance has inspired images of community, activity, and many small lights gathered together.

name: Double Cluster
astronomy: The Double Cluster consists of the adjacent open clusters NGC 869 and NGC 884 in Perseus.
symbolism: Two neighboring stellar gatherings offer a cultural image of parallel paths and paired perspectives.

name: Omega Centauri
astronomy: Omega Centauri is the largest and brightest globular cluster visible from Earth, containing millions of stars.
symbolism: Its dense globe of light can symbolize accumulated time and a multitude held in one form.

name: 47 Tucanae
astronomy: 47 Tucanae is a bright globular cluster near the Small Magellanic Cloud in the southern sky.
symbolism: Its compact glow near another galaxy creates a cultural image of neighboring scales and quiet abundance.

name: Hercules Cluster
astronomy: The Hercules Cluster, Messier 13, is a prominent globular cluster in the constellation Hercules.
symbolism: A distant sphere made of countless stars can evoke collective memory and the depth hidden in a faint patch of sky.

name: Crab Nebula
astronomy: The Crab Nebula, Messier 1, is a supernova remnant energized by a pulsar at its center.
symbolism: Its expanding filaments are a cultural image of traces that remain after a dramatic celestial change.

name: Lagoon Nebula
astronomy: The Lagoon Nebula, Messier 8, is a large emission nebula and star-forming region in Sagittarius.
symbolism: Its layered gas and dust offer an image of depth, shelter, and hidden stellar formation.

name: Eagle Nebula
astronomy: The Eagle Nebula, Messier 16, is an emission nebula and young open cluster known for the Pillars of Creation.
symbolism: Its pillar-like dust structures have become a cultural image of formation shaped slowly by light.

name: Ring Nebula
astronomy: The Ring Nebula, Messier 57, is a planetary nebula formed from material shed by a dying Sun-like star.
symbolism: Its circular outline can evoke cycles, enclosing forms, and visible transformation.

name: Helix Nebula
astronomy: The Helix Nebula is a large, nearby planetary nebula in Aquarius, created by an evolved Sun-like star.
symbolism: Its eye-like ring has inspired cultural images of observation and a window into stellar change.

name: Carina Nebula
astronomy: The Carina Nebula is a vast southern star-forming complex containing massive young stars and Eta Carinae.
symbolism: Its sculpted clouds offer a cultural image of making, turbulence, and immense scale.

name: Horsehead Nebula
astronomy: The Horsehead Nebula is a dark nebula in Orion silhouetted against glowing hydrogen gas.
symbolism: Its recognizable silhouette is a cultural reminder that dark space can define a pattern as clearly as light.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
astronomy: The Triangulum Galaxy, Messier 33, is a spiral galaxy in the Local Group and a neighbor of Andromeda and the Milky Way.
symbolism: Its place among nearby galaxies can suggest a triangle of relationships across enormous distance.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
astronomy: The Whirlpool Galaxy, Messier 51, is an interacting spiral galaxy with a smaller companion galaxy.
symbolism: Its visible spiral and companion offer a cultural image of pattern, encounter, and motion on a grand scale.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
astronomy: The Sombrero Galaxy, Messier 104, is a galaxy with a bright central bulge and a prominent dark dust lane.
symbolism: The contrast of bright bulge and dark band can evoke layers, boundaries, and a composed silhouette.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud
astronomy: The Large Magellanic Cloud is a dwarf irregular galaxy that orbits the Milky Way and is visible from the southern hemisphere.
symbolism: Its cloud-like appearance beside the Milky Way has made it a cultural image of a companion light beyond the familiar band.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud
astronomy: The Small Magellanic Cloud is a dwarf irregular galaxy and a satellite of the Milky Way.
symbolism: Its faint separate glow can evoke quiet proximity and the presence of smaller neighboring worlds.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy
astronomy: The Pinwheel Galaxy, Messier 101, is a large face-on spiral galaxy in Ursa Major with many star-forming regions.
symbolism: Its open spiral arms create a cultural image of a pattern unfolding outward from a bright center.

name: Cigar Galaxy
astronomy: The Cigar Galaxy, Messier 82, is a starburst galaxy with intense star formation triggered by gravitational interaction.
symbolism: Its bright elongated form can evoke intensity, compression, and the visible energy of interaction.
